The mayor made a short speech, the musicians played until the lanterns burned low, and the travelers, tired and dusty, were given the warmest room at the inn. In the days that followed, the blacksmith repaired their cart, the baker sent fresh loaves each morning, and the children brought flowers from the meadow. When at last the road was clear, the whole village gathered to say goodbye. The two of them promised to return before the harvest, climbed onto the wagon, and waved until the rooftops disappeared behind the hill.
